events.label: birth
events.text: Amalric born to King Fulk and Queen Melisende.

evidence.quote: Amalric was born in 1136 to King Fulk

events.text: Given the County of Jaffa as apanage on reaching majority.

evidence.quote: Amalric , who had been given the County of Jaffa as an apanage when he reached the age of majority in 1151

events.text: Ascalon captured by Baldwin III and added to Amalric's fief of Jaffa.

evidence.quote: In 1153 Baldwin captured the Egyptian fortress of Ascalon , which was then added to Amalrics fief of Jaffa
Amalric married Agnes of Courtenay in 1157

events.label: expedition
events.text: First expedition into Egypt over unpaid Fatimid tribute.

evidence.quote: Amalric led his first expedition into Egypt in 1163

events.text: Marriage to Agnes of Courtenay annulled as condition for accession

evidence.quote: Baldwin III died on 10 February 1163
Amalric agreed and ascended the throne without a wife

events.text: Ascended the throne as King of Jerusalem after Baldwin III's death.

evidence.quote: Baldwin III died on 10 February 1163 and the kingdom passed to Amalric

events.label: expedition
events.text: Returned to Egypt and besieged Shirkuh at Bilbeis.

evidence.quote: Amalric returned to Egypt in 1164 and besieged Shirkuh in Bilbeis

events.label: ransom
events.text: Secured the ransom of captive Bohemund III of Antioch.

evidence.quote: secured Bohemunds ransom in 1165

events.label: diplomacy
events.text: Sent envoys to Byzantium seeking an alliance and a Byzantine wife.

evidence.quote: The year 1166 was relatively quiet , but Amalric sent envoys to the Byzantine Empire

events.label: expedition
events.text: Followed Shirkuh into Egypt; treaty with caliph al-Adid; Alexandria siege.

evidence.quote: In 1167 , Nur ad-Din sent Shirkuh back to Egypt and Amalric once again followed him
marry Maria in Tyre on August 29 , 1167

events.label: alliance
events.text: Negotiated an alliance with Byzantine emperor Manuel against Egypt.

evidence.quote: In 1168 Amalric and Manuel negotiated an alliance against Egypt

events.label: invasion
events.text: Invaded Egypt without Byzantine aid and seized Bilbeis.

evidence.quote: In October , without waiting for any Byzantine assistance

events.label: invasion
events.text: Launched another invasion of Egypt and besieged Damietta.

evidence.quote: in October Amalric launched yet another invasion and besieged Damietta

events.label: visit
events.text: Visited Constantinople in person seeking help against Saladin.

evidence.quote: in 1171 Amalric visited Constantinople himself

events.label: siege
events.text: Immediately besieged Banias after Nur ad-Din's death.

evidence.quote: Nur ad-Din died in 1174 , upon which Amalric immediately besieged Banias

events.label: death
events.text: Died of fever in Jerusalem; succeeded by son Baldwin IV.

evidence.quote: he died on July 11
The leprous child Baldwin IV succeeded his father

undated_mentions: Took up the regency of Antioch and Tripoli after Bohemund III was captured (c.1164-65, no explicit date).
Besieged in the Tower of David with his mother Melisende during the civil war with Baldwin III.
Alexandria handed over to Amalric after Shirkuh's negotiated peace (1167, no explicit date).
Commissioned William of Tyre to write a history of the kingdom (around 1167).
Acre reverted to the royal domain after Theodora eloped (around 1167).
Sent Frederick de la Roche to Europe to seek help against Saladin (1169, no explicit date).
Marched to Cairo and retreated after Shawar offered two million gold (1168, no explicit date).
Signed a truce with Saladin ending the Damietta siege and returned home (no explicit date).
Bequeathed Nablus to Maria Comnena and Isabella on his deathbed (1174).
